identity.title: Murphy sign (inspiratory arrest on RUQ palpation)

technique.how: Place fingertips under the right costal margin at the mid-clavicular line while the patient exhales, then ask for a deep breath. The sign is positive when inspiration is abruptly halted by pain as the gallbladder descends onto the examining hand; compare with the left side, which should not arrest breathing.
technique.prerequisites: Cooperative patient able to take a deep breath; examine before opioid analgesia if possible.

interpretation.positive_finding: Inspiratory arrest with RUQ pain raises the probability of acute cholecystitis (pooled LR+ 2.8, wide CI) and in one ED series was present in 97% of patients with a positive HIDA scan.
interpretation.negative_finding: A negative Murphy sign lowers probability modestly and does not exclude cholecystitis, especially in the elderly or after analgesia.
interpretation.pitfalls: Frequently undocumented; sensitivity falls in elderly and opioid-treated patients; hepatitis, hepatic congestion and right lower lobe pneumonia can produce a false-positive. Sonographic Murphy sign is a separate finding.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive with RUQ pain/fever: obtain RUQ ultrasound and start cholecystitis pathway. Negative: does not remove need for imaging if pretest probability is meaningful.

estimates.population: Adults with abdominal pain or suspected acute cholecystitis (17 pooled studies)
estimates.reference_standard: Surgery, pathology, HIDA scan, RUQ ultrasound or consistent clinical course

estimates.population: 100 consecutive ED patients referred for urgent HIDA scan; sign documented in 65
estimates.quote: The presence of Murphy's sign was both sensitive (97.2%) and highly predictive (93.3%) of a positive HBS

sources.citation: Trowbridge RL, Rutkowski NK, Shojania KG. Does this patient have acute cholecystitis? JAMA. 2003;289(1):80-86.

Singer AJ, McCracken G, Henry MC, Thode HC Jr, Cabahug CJ. Correlation among clinical, laboratory, and hepatobiliary scanning findings in patients with suspected acute cholecystitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1996;28(3):267-272.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative sign to exclude cholecystitis in elderly, diabetic, or opioid-treated patients, or in suspected cholangitis (fever, jaundice) where imaging and blood cultures are needed regardless.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: RUQ pain with fever, jaundice, or hypotension suggests cholangitis or gangrenous cholecystitis: blood cultures, IV antibiotics, urgent imaging and surgical/GI review.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: RCE pooled CI crosses 1.0; Singer 1996 found the sign undocumented in 35% of charts, indicating inconsistent elicitation.

extraction_notes: RCE pooled LR+ 2.8 (0.8-8.6) taken from the abstract; the RCE table (with LR- and per-study sens/spec) is not accessible via PubMed/PMC. Singer 1996 is retrospective, ED-based, with HIDA as reference and 35 undocumented cases (verification bias); specificity not given in abstract so only sensitivity entered. PPV 93.3% not entered as a stat field.
